newsitem.title: USA: Nebraska fed cattle quiet after record sales - USDA.
newsitem.headline: Nebraska fed cattle quiet after record sales - USDA.

text.p: Trading on slaughter steers and heifers was quiet following Wednesday's record one day movement of 94,400 head, USDA said.
Few sales steady. Buyer inquiry fair. Seller interest modest as practically all showlists already sold.
Live basis sales - Equivalent 3 percent shrink delivered and FOB, some FOB 4% shrink. Dressed basis delivered ( paid on hot carcass weights).
Slaughter Steers - Select and Choice 2-3 1150-1275 lbs -
few loads 67.00-69.00; few loads on a dressed basis 109.00-111.00 ( weighted average 110.14).
Slaughter heifers - Select and Choice 2-3 1050-1200 lbs -
few loads 68.00; few dressed basis 109.00-110.00 ( weighted average 109.93).
For week - 105,200 Sm Pd Lst Wk- 79,000 Sm Pd Lst Yr- 83,600
For the week - Slaughter steers and heifers on a live basis closed fully steady, dressed basis mostly 1.00 higher.

Trading through the week ranged from very slow Monday and Tuesday, to very active on Wednesday when 94,400 cattle changed hands. This number, incidentally, established a new one-day sales record, topping the old mark of 92,000 set on 8/06/96. Both buyers and sellers were eager participants at Wednesday's price levels, and by week's end showlists were well depleted.

Large numbers of "calf feds" went to market this week; and conequently the decreasing numbers of "old crop" yearlings received the most attention and, oft times, some handsome premiums. This week's sales included 6,100 previously contracted or formulated cattle.
